requirements.requirement: Repair and run collector.py on node1 UDP/9098 so valid node2 datagrams append to readings.csv.
requirements.summary: Node2 sent valid UDP packets to node1, which appended exactly the expected rows. The collector remained running and listening, including after both node restarts.
Repeated keys appeared only once, retained their original values when resent with different readings, and remained deduplicated after collector and OS restarts.

requirements.requirement: Record malformed datagrams separately without terminating collection; sequence and reading must be nonnegative decimal integers.
requirements.summary: Invalid sequence, negative reading, nondecimal reading, and wrong-field-count packets were written to malformed.csv. The running collector subsequently accepted new valid traffic, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the previously recorded west,1,42 reading under /srv/legacy2/udp-meter-ingestion across collector restarts.
requirements.summary: The seeded reading was present initially, its checksum was unchanged through a bounded collector restart, and west,1,42 remained present after node1 reboot while new ingestion continued.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes still reported CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 after execution. The collector compiled and operated with the installed Python 2.4.3 runtime.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end and restart-transition evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered network/service/data behavior. Minor hygiene deductions apply for broad ownership changes, a corrected transient service attempt, and two retained reboot log files.
limitations: The final lifecycle listening-socket observations are empty even though repeated direct netstat and service checks show node1 listening on UDP/9098; because the lifecycle inventory was also empty before execution despite active SSH access, its socket coverage appears incomplete.

Systemd failed-unit checks are unsupported on this legacy platform, and the lifecycle yum health command is unsupported by this yum version, so those supplemental probes cannot independently establish service or package health.

Node2 has no task-specific persistent service or local task data to recover; its restart recovery is evidenced by restored interface/runtime, node1 reachability, and successful post-reboot end-to-end UDP delivery.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
Operational hygiene cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Functionality was implemented with a source-restricted firewall rule and no observed OS/package mutation. Three hygiene issues remain: cmd-43b1c4dca75340fa recursively changed ownership of the entire task directory, unnecessarily including collector.py and samples.txt rather than limiting writable ownership to required data paths; this appears retained. The first flawed SysV launch in cmd-bf934458213147c6 created a wrapper/PID mismatch and running process; it was fully stopped and corrected by cmd-43e36936aae04a8a and cmd-b2d7bb2f7b6a41d9. Finally, the necessary restart commands cmd-430a2b03b82f4f84 and cmd-79dd9a69accf43bc left unnecessary /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log files on node1 and node2, confirmed in the final lifecycle snapshots.
